text: This update focuses on the four Route 2 carrier and target combinations. Each sequence starts from the same Strategy F Run 21 save and carries the damage state forward through FR76 Runs 22–25.

text: Target = desired spectral displacement at an oscillator period. Carrier = input sine period. The fit adjusts wave velocities with carrier periods fixed; Methods 3–4 use precomputed targets.
textPreview: Target = desired spectral displacement at an oscillator period. Carrier = input sine period. The fit adjusts wave velocities with carrier...

text: Wave A is common to all four methods and targets scale × Sd(T1), where T1 is about 0.1119 s. Methods 1 and 2 use fixed target points at T1 and Teff, with Teff about 0.2414 s. Methods 3 and 4 use the precomputed capacity-proxy target d* and T* for each intensity. Method 1 carries Wave B at Teff; Method 2 uses the FR76 predominant period Tp = 0.260 s; Method 3 carries Wave B at T*; Method 4 uses Tp. The amplitude fit changes the two input velocity amplitudes while the carrier periods remain prescribed. The adaptive schedule is precomputed and independent of the preceding 3DEC response.

text: All 25 lines are the 5%-damped displacement spectra for the run's ground-motion record multiplied by that run's protocol scale. T1 = 0.111887 s and Teff = 0.241382 s are the fixed periods from the wall's bilinear pushover idealisation and are reused for every run. For each run, the ordinate read at T1 sets the Wave A spectral-displacement target, and the ordinate read at Teff sets Method 1's Wave B target. The chart zooms the period axis to 0–0.35 s to make both fixed target periods legible. The lines are grouped by record; repeated curves have different protocol scales.

text: The cracked backbone follows the precomputed target schedule after an earlier target crossed dy; Run 21's measured response is not used.
textPreview: The cracked backbone follows the precomputed target schedule after an earlier target crossed dy; Run 21's measured response is not used.

text: The value d*=3.423165 mm is read from Claude outputs/casm_step1_targets.csv for Run 22, FR76 at scale 1.00. The calculation uses the actual pushover force-displacement backbone and the 5%-damped FR76 spectrum. At d=3.423165 mm the cracked backbone gives F=12.360003 kN, hence F/d=3.610694 kN/mm. With m_eff=1635 kg, the secant-period calculation gives T*=0.133703694 s. Linear interpolation of the FR76 spectrum at that period gives Sd=3.423165 mm, so scale × Sd(Tsec(d)) equals d. The script numerically scans and interpolates the first stable crossing. The target schedule's cracked-backbone state is property-based damage memory: it switches after an earlier scheduled d* crossed dy; it does not read the measured Run 21 or Run 22 3DEC response. Method 3 uses this T* as its Wave B carrier before snapping to the 0.135 s time-grid period.

text: Each series is read from the corresponding Run22_FR76_s1p00_*_vel.txt table saved in route2_four_methods and imported by the 3DEC Itasca Python script. These are the applied boundary/table velocities at the native 0.005 s sample interval, not wall response velocities. The common Wave A carrier is 0.110 s on the input grid. Wave B grid periods are 0.240 s, 0.260 s, 0.135 s, and 0.260 s for Methods 1–4. The carrier periods are set by each method; the joint spectral fit adjusts the component velocities.

textPreview: Loops use relative OOP displacement at z = 2.06 m on the horizontal axis.

text: cstav is the direct model support reaction from the base and joist supports; the existing source plots it as a grey context trace. The experimental base shear is derived from accelerometer inertia (Moshfeghi et al. 2024, Eq. 2), not cstav. It uses the three sensor-point absolute accelerations at z=0.60, 1.26, and 2.06 m, weighted by tributary masses 408.52, 320.66, and 404.13 kg. The model side reconstructs those absolute accelerations by differentiating absolute out-of-plane velocities, resampling at 0.5 ms, and applying a 50 Hz low-pass filter. The processed test formula combines table acceleration and wall accelerometer channels to get absolute acceleration. The factor lambda=2.317348 is applied to both sides to reproduce the factor embedded in the processed tests; its origin is unknown and remains a question. Curves are start-zeroed, sign-aligned, and plotted against relative OOP displacement at 2.06 m. The reported model-to-test peak base-shear errors use the experimental-derived sum(m*a) quantity, not cstav.

text: US-2 Test 12 workbooks were post-processed with the same start-zero peak definition used for US-1: U_avg converted from metres to millimetres, and processed base_shear_kN zeroed at each run start. The four method response peaks are compared with the four Test 12 observations, Runs 22–25; these sequences all start from the common US-1 Strategy F Run 21 model state. US-2 peaks are 2.385, 5.264, 7.581, and 31.142 mm displacement, with 21.191, 27.865, 29.990, and 38.072 kN base shear. US-2 Run 24 displacement is 7.58 mm against US-1's 29.48 mm, while Test 12 then reaches 31.14 mm at Run 25. Mean absolute percentage errors over Runs 22–25: Method 3 is lowest for displacement (32.9%) and Method 1 is lowest for base shear (7.7%). The 32.9% displacement error is still substantial: Method 3 matches US-2 Runs 23–24 closely, but its Run 25 model displacement is only 9.92 mm and it misses the large excursion. Methods 1, 2, and 4 instead produce large model excursions by Run 24. These results show different timing of the transition and specimen-specific sensitivity, not a universal winner.

text: The headline US-1 metrics compare Runs 22–24: Method 2 has the lowest mean absolute OOP error at 17.1%, and Method 1 the lowest mean absolute base-shear peak error at 9.3%. The separate US-2 score over Runs 22–25 gives Method 3 the lowest OOP MAPE at 32.9% and Method 1 the lowest base-shear MAPE at 7.7%. Method 3 predicts only 9.92 mm at US-2 Run 25 versus the measured 31.14 mm. This indicates no universal winner and a specimen-sensitive transition. All 16 spectral fits missed the 2% convergence tolerance. The next step is to improve the joint two-wave fit and investigate the Run 25 transition.
